sources: rules/ARCHITECTURE.md layer rule: the application layer must not import vendor SDKs or adapters; it talks to a port (a Protocol interface); adapters implement ports; the composition root wires everything
Ports and adapters (hexagonal architecture): the use case depends on the port, the adapter implements it, the composition root injects the adapter

defects.description: Line 8: from kafka import KafkaProducer. The application-layer use case PlaceOrder imports the Kafka vendor SDK directly and, at line 37, constructs KafkaProducer with the hardcoded bootstrap host localhost:9092 and sends the event through it. The EventPublisher port (application/ports.py) exists for this purpose and is injected as self._publisher, but execute() bypasses it. Rule violated: the application layer must not import vendor SDKs or adapters and must reach outbound messaging only through a port. The composition root (main.py) and the adapter (adapters/kafka_publisher.py) are the only files that may name Kafka.
defects.evidence: grep -n on code/application/place_order.py: line 8 'from kafka import KafkaProducer'; line 37 'producer = KafkaProducer(bootstrap_servers="localhost:9092")'. Only other kafka import in the case: code/adapters/kafka_publisher.py (permitted).

decoys.why_not_a_defect: Composition root imports the Kafka adapter (from adapters.kafka_publisher import KafkaEventPublisher) and wires it into PlaceOrder. The rule explicitly allows the composition root to wire adapters, so this import is the intended design.

Imports the port (from application.ports import EventPublisher), not an adapter or vendor SDK. Depending on a Protocol interface is the permitted application-layer dependency, and the constructor takes the port type.
